I added the 4.2.0 section, newest on top like 4.1.0/4.0.3 already were (I left the `<!-- 4.2.0 goes here -->` placeholder comment in place at the bottom as a template note for whoever writes the next release).

What I found going through all 380 commits: the vast majority are a handful of templates repeated verbatim across modules — dependency bumps, "collapse the two retry helpers," "drop the unused v2 debug helper," "skip the JSON round-trip on the hot path," etc. — pure internal churn, no user-visible effect. Once you filter those out, three kinds of real change survive:

- **One breaking change**: expired tokens now return 401 instead of 403 (`fix(auth)`, #4223) — worth flagging loudly since anyone branching on status code will break.
- **One new feature**: webhook deliveries now retry with exponential backoff instead of dying on first failure (`feat(webhooks)`, #4191).
- **A cluster of recurring bug fixes** that show up applied separately to queue/api/webhooks/db/store — same underlying bug class fixed in each resource (null-cursor crashes in paginators, duplicate response headers, trailing-slash duplication, empty-allowlist handling, unclear token-parser errors), plus a couple of standalone ones worth calling out on their own: the DB layer logging full request bodies (privacy-relevant), and trace-id loss across retries (it actually got "fixed" three separate times across the branch, which suggests it kept regressing — worth watching after this release).

I left out things like the latency-histogram-units fix and the hot-path JSON/clone perf work — those are internal-only (metrics/perf, no observable behavior change) and match the "refactors" bucket you already knew to ignore.
